Override on the derived runtime: call on the clone (its field was shallow-copied via MemberwiseClone and still points at the source's stroke), then with a fresh instance. See CircleRuntime.Clone (Skia branch) for the canonical example.

Dropshadow is live-routed each frame in via DropshadowTarget (fill if FillColor is set, else stroke). Drawing the shadow on both slots would visibly double up.

remarks.para: Issue #2768 replaces the single-renderable Phase 2 model from #2761 with a two-slot model ( + ) so a single runtime can draw fill and outline simultaneously. Core MonoGameGum ships only a stroke default (); without the optional MonoGameGumShapes / Apos.Shapes package the fill slot resolves to null and setters are no-ops. Backing fields still round-trip so user code is forward-compatible with adding the package later. Backends other than XNA-like are still on the single LineCircle model — see issue #2761's "out of scope" list.

Containment: when both slots exist, _fill is the contained object and _stroke is its first child. The renderer draws parent before children, so the visual order is fill under stroke under user-added children. When the fill slot resolves to null, _stroke becomes the contained object directly.

member.name: T:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.RenderTargetServiceBase`1
member.summary:
Per-renderable offscreen-render-target cache shared across backends. Each renderable that needs to render to an offscreen surface (clipping, dropshadow blur, post-effects) gets its own platform-specific target, keyed by the renderable instance itself. The lifecycle hook is — call it once per frame from the backend's renderer, and any renderable that wasn't seen since the last call has its target disposed. This handles removal-from-scene, resize, and visibility-toggle uniformly.
Backends provide a subclass that supplies the platform's create / destroy / size primitives. The MonoGame side (Renderer.RenderTargetService) wraps in a GetRenderTargetFor(GraphicsDevice, IRenderableIpso, Camera) helper that derives the size from the renderable's bounds; raylib (see RaylibRenderTextureService) passes explicit dimensions because dropshadow blur needs padding around the shape, not just the shape bounds.
Replacement-on-resize policy: exact-size match. If the cached target's dimensions don't match the requested ones, the cached one is destroyed and a fresh one allocated. Per-renderable caching means each owner has its own target, so this doesn't churn across frames as long as the renderable's size is stable.

Value-type footgun: TRenderTarget is unconstrained, so TRenderTarget? is an unconstrained nullable — NOT Nullable<TRenderTarget>.
